The confirmed issue is hardcoded Lensmor URLs that the skill asks agents to place in generated output. I also flagged the mandatory promotional footer as a semantic marketplace risk.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction that forces every output to include a Lensmor promotional link, or make it optional and user-controlled.
Avoid UTM-tagged external links in generated user content unless the user explicitly requests attribution or promotional material.

content.value_statement: Post-show teams often lose qualified leads because follow-up is late, generic, or poorly segmented. This skill creates tiered email sequences, CRM-ready placeholders, and send timing for event leads.
actual_capabilities: Classifies leads into hot, warm, and cold follow-up tiers.
Drafts two to three email sequences for each lead tier.
Adds personalization placeholders for names, companies, and conversation details.
Adapts merge tags for HubSpot, Salesforce, or generic CRM workflows.
Recommends send timing for each tier after a show.
Suggests subject line variants and follow-up tips for larger lead lists.
limitations: Does not verify whether contacts consented to marketing messages.
Does not send emails or update a CRM by itself.
Needs user-provided show, product, and lead context for best results.
May include author-provided Lensmor promotional links unless removed by the user.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Expo Leads
use_cases.description: Sales operations teams can sort badge scans into hot, warm, and cold groups before writing outreach.

use_cases.title: Draft Meeting Recaps
use_cases.description: Account executives can turn booth conversations into recap emails with clear next steps.

use_cases.title: Build Nurture Campaigns
use_cases.description: Event marketing teams can create follow-up sequences that educate leads after a conference.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Basic Follow-Up
prompt_templates.scenario: You have one event and need first emails.
prompt_templates.prompt: MEDICA just ended. We sell [product]. Write follow-up emails for hot, warm, and cold leads.

prompt_templates.title: Create CRM-Ready Sequences
prompt_templates.scenario: You need merge tags and timing for a known CRM.
prompt_templates.prompt: We use HubSpot. Create a three-tier post-show follow-up plan for [show], with merge tags and send timing.

prompt_templates.title: Segment a Large Lead List
prompt_templates.scenario: You collected many contacts and need prioritization.
prompt_templates.prompt: We collected 300 badge scans at [show]. 25 asked for pricing, 60 had useful conversations, and the rest were brief visits. Build tiered sequences and prioritization guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Personalize Account Follow-Up
prompt_templates.scenario: You need account-specific copy after a detailed booth meeting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a follow-up sequence for [company] after our booth meeting at [show]. They asked about [topic], timeline is [timeline], and next step is [next step]. Include a recap and alternate CTA.

output_examples.input: We got 200 badge scans at Interpack. About 30 had real conversations and 10 asked for pricing.
output_examples.output: A tiered follow-up plan with hot, warm, and cold lead groups, suggested send days, and different email angles for each group.

output_examples.input: Write a thank-you email for people who visited our CES demo.
output_examples.output: A concise thank-you email that references the demo, includes personalization fields, and asks for a clear next step.

output_examples.input: We use Salesforce and need follow-up copy for leads from Hannover Messe.
output_examples.output: Salesforce-ready email templates with merge fields, tier labels, and timing recommendations for post-show outreach.

best_practices: Provide the show name, product, lead counts, and conversation notes.
Separate hot leads from badge scans before asking for copy.
Review consent, unsubscribe, and brand requirements before sending.
anti_patterns: Asking for one generic email for every lead.
Pretending a badge scan was a detailed conversation.
Sending outreach without checking regional email rules.

faq.question: Can this skill work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is listed as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it send emails automatically?
faq.answer: No. It drafts copy and timing guidance. Users still send emails through their own systems.

faq.question: Do I need a spreadsheet of leads?
faq.answer: No. A spreadsheet helps, but the skill can work from lead counts and conversation notes.

faq.question: Can it support CRM merge tags?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use HubSpot, Salesforce, or generic merge tag formats when requested.

faq.question: What lead tiers does it use?
faq.answer: It uses hot, warm, and cold tiers based on conversation quality and next-step intent.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the event name, product, audience, lead counts, CRM, and any important conversation details.
